answer: Each identity stakes 80 credits for a timber booth in the atlas. A beacon draws 5% of booths each epoch: the examiner's prism prompt splits its last job into three questions, answerable with the signing key in ten minutes. A miss freezes the bond and publishes it in the atlas. Fakes need one sitter per timber booth at 30 credits per epoch, as booths run together: the kth fake costs 30 plus 80 locked, so 1,000 lock 80,000, pay 30,000 per epoch; one honest agent pays 80 once. A rented sitter fails on the prism prompt's unsigned history; auditors replay it against the key.
